thread:
erin.support: FYI support ticket #9382 — customer reports intermittent 401s when calling our /v1/generate and a sudden jump in token usage billing yesterday evening. They included a small traceback and request-id.

alice.srsec: Thanks Erin. Any overlap with the redteam pen test window? We just received a report about possible KMS alias enumeration via chained STS in one of our test accounts. Could be unrelated but worth correlating.

erin.support: Ticket timestamps: 2026-03-15T21:12:03Z to 2026-03-15T22:00:11Z. The customer attached request-ids: r-34ab2c and r-34ab9f. Billing spike was ~11:07PM UTC.

bob.eng: I can look at the request-ids. If it's a 401 it might be an auth token expiry or a bad refresh flow. The billing spike could be retries + longer context length.

sam.billing: On the billing side I see an anomalous increase in generation tokens for that customer around the same time — +300% in 30m. The account also had several failed auth attempts from the same IP block (ASN 13335).

alice.srsec: Redteam evidence: they ran a short repro in a staging tenant and chained STS to assume an infra role, then used `aws kms list-aliases` and `kms:DescribeKey` to enumerate. They claim no decrypt allowed. However, they also found a session policy bug that allowed a reused session tag to persist across assume-role calls. If session tagging can be abused, it could lead to anomalous access.

carla.devops: Re: session tags — we recently deployed an optimization that reuses cached STS tokens for infra-runner. That could explain stale tag baggage. I'll find the deploy and roll back if needed.

dave.research: From a risk perspective: listing aliases + DescribeKey is information disclosure. If alias names include tenant IDs or feature flags, that's P2. If it's only internal names, P3. But combined with auth anomalies + billing spike, we should treat as P2 until proven otherwise.

erin.support: Customer wants immediate reassurance. They asked "was any data exposed?" We need a quick statement.

alice.srsec: Short answer to CS: No evidence of Decrypt or GenerateDataKey being successful from the redteam steps. We saw ListAliases/DescribeKey only. But we need to correlate with the customer's request-ids and CloudTrail to be sure.

bob.eng: Searching logs for those request-ids... Found r-34ab2c: origin IP 18.205.33.12, user-agent rwd-sdk-js/1.4.2, auth error 401: ExpiredToken. r-34ab9f: success but long latency (1.2s) and unusually large prompt (25k tokens) — probably responsible for billing spike.

sam.billing: The long prompt matches the customer's usage pattern (they do long analytics runs). The failed 401s were from a different subdomain using an older SDK. Might be a token refresh bug. Not seeing KMS involvement here yet.

alice.srsec: I'll pull CloudTrail across KMS and STS for the 2-hour window and search for `ListAliases` and cross-reference assumerole ARNs. Need to know if any calls used production key ARNs.

carla.devops: Found a recent IAM inline policy that grants `kms:ListAliases` to role `rwd-infra-runner` in prod for debugging. I think that's the one redteam exploited in staging; it also exists in prod due to a terraform drift we missed.

bob.eng: If prod has `ListAliases` allowed broadly, that's bad. Even if no decrypt, it's a compliance hit if aliases leak tenant ids. We should add a conditional deny for prod roles now and plan a terraform fix.

carla.devops: I can patch prod role to add an explicit Deny for `kms:ListAliases` and `kms:DescribeKey` pending terraform correction. Doing a small scoped change to reduce blast radius. Will schedule for the next maintenance window but can emergency patch if SOC authorizes.

infra-bot: change: IAM inline policy update queued by carla.devops for role `rwd-infra-runner` — https://ci.internal/runs/801

alice.srsec: While we wait, I'll request CloudTrail retention snapshot and export relevant events to s3://rwd-security-evidence/1976543210/ so support and legal can review. Also pinging compliance for potential data retention concerns.

dave.research: Also check HSM logs — if DescribeKey runs against keys on HSM-backed keystore, there may be additional metadata in HSM audit logs. Coordinate with key ops.

carla.devops: Emergency patch applied to prod role at 2026-03-16T00:45:10Z. Deny rules added for `kms:ListAliases` and `kms:DescribeKey` for that role. See commit rwd/terraform@d9e7b2.

redteam-bot: Acknowledged. We'll re-run a constrained repro against prod test account tomorrow morning and share findings.

erin.support: Sent customer an interim update: "No evidence of decryption or data exfiltration. We identified a permissions configuration we are hardening and will follow up after we finish the audit."

alice.srsec: Post-patch observations: CloudTrail shows `ListAliases` calls from the suspect role now returning AccessDenied. No DescribeKey successes recorded during the window. Exported parity logs uploaded: s3://rwd-security-evidence/1976543210/cloudtrail-parity.json

sam.billing: Billing spike reconciled — caused by a long prompt run and retries due to SDK refresh issues. We'll follow up with the SDK team to patch token refresh logic. No billing fraud detected.

dave.research: Final severity: P2 initially, downgraded to P3 after prod hardening and no evidence of DescribeKey/Decrypt. Recommend: terraform module change to remove `kms:ListAliases`/`DescribeKey` from standard infra roles, audit aliases for tenant IDs, add a CI lint to block alias patterns containing customer identifiers.

bob.eng: I'll open the terraform PR and include a migration plan for any teams that relied on `ListAliases` for debugging.

erin.support: Closing support ticket if customer doesn't respond within 72h. Drafted external-safe summary for CS.

alice.srsec: Notes saved to incident tracker: INC-2026-0316-01. Retest scheduled with redteam tomorrow at 09:00 UTC. Closing thread for now — reach out if anything pops up. :lock:
summary: Redteam reported KMS alias enumeration path; support reported auth 401s and billing spike. Investigated and correlated logs. Found IAM policy granting kms:ListAliases to infra role in prod (drift). Patched prod to deny ListAliases/DescribeKey, exported CloudTrail evidence, billing spike traced to long prompt + SDK token refresh bug. Redteam retest pending; initial severity P2 -> downgraded to P3 post-fix. Actions: terraform module updates, alias audit, CI lint, SDK fix.
